# dsh-token-monitor

**The whole plugin except this sentence was generated by DeepSeek Harness**

A floating monitor for DeepSeek Harness: your **account balance**, the **tokens this conversation has consumed**, and the **estimated cost** of the conversation at DeepSeek's official rates.

A slim tab docked to the right edge of the window, expanding into a small card. Draggable, collapsible, out of the way while you read.

> 中文说明: [README.md](./README.md) · Repo: [GitHub](https://github.com/Ta9y/dsh-token-monitor)

```
┌──────────────────────┐ ┌──┐
│ ● Your chat title  × │ │¥ │
│ Balance     ¥25.87   │ │25│
│ This chat  ≈¥0.42 25.4M│ │.8│
└──────────────────────┘ └──┘
        hover to expand ↑
```

## Features

- **Balance** — read through DeepSeek's account service; hover to see the bonus wallet
- **Conversation usage** — sums `usage` over every model call in the session
- **Conversation cost** — estimated from the official price list, per model and per **peak / off-peak** window
- **Search / Fetch billing** — counts `web_search` / `web_fetch` calls at the official ¥5 per 1,000
  (DeepSeek states these are **free until 2026-11-01 00:00**; the plugin only bills them from that date on)
- **Monthly price refresh** — scraped from the official page, cached for 30 days, old values kept on failure
- **Follows the active conversation** — switching chats refreshes immediately
- **Follows the app language** — Simplified Chinese / English, switched live
- **Draggable** — drag the tab or the card; they stay vertically aligned, position stored as a viewport ratio
- **Unobtrusive** — details appear after a 320 ms hover; hovering the close row never expands them

## ⚠️ High-risk permission usage (must read)

1. **This project requests no elevated, approval, or proxy-operation permission.** It registers no tools, never
   auto-approves, never bypasses or weakens any approval policy, and never needs an "Allow once" click.
2. **What it reads**: usage data for the current conversation and its child sessions (balance, usage, title,
   context, team roster). After a child finishes it reads that child's on-disk session log once, only to add up tokens.
3. **What it serves**: three read-only routes — `/dsh-token-monitor/state`, `/dsh-token-monitor/probe`,
   `/dsh-token-monitor/ui.js` — on DSH's own loopback, guarded by a random token plus same-origin / desktop Origin
   checks; cross-site requests get `403`.
4. **What it writes**: only `debug.log` (diagnostics), `token.txt` (page token) and `prices.auto.json` (price cache)
   inside the plugin directory. It never writes to the workspace or to sessions.
5. **Does it call out?** Only the monthly price-page fetch (`api-docs.deepseek.com`); balance goes through DSH's own
   account service, the plugin never talks to the platform directly.
6. **It uploads nothing**: no telemetry, no analytics, no third-party API; data stays in local process memory.

The per-interface table with frequencies is in [Permissions & interfaces](#permissions--interfaces) below.

## Requirements

- DSH 0.2.x (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app` composition)
- Desktop uses the `dsh.client` module path; plain browser mode (`dsh web`) uses index injection
- Tested on Windows with the `desktop` profile only; macOS / Linux unverified

## Install

The plugin is a standard DSH bundle with both a host half (`index.js`) and a client half (`client.js`).

> Replace `<profile>` with the profile you install into — `desktop` for the desktop app.
> `dsh plugin` forwards its arguments to pnpm, so any spec pnpm understands works.

### A. Straight from GitHub (recommended — the only one-command install that works today)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Ta9y/dsh-token-monitor
```

### B. Through the UI

**Settings → Plugins → Install**, paste `github:Ta9y/dsh-token-monitor`.

### C. Manually (handy while developing)

```powershell
cd $HOME\.dsh\profiles\desktop
pnpm add file:C:/path/to/dsh-token-monitor
```

Then add `dsh-token-monitor` to the `dsh.profile.bundles` array in that directory's `package.json`.

### D. From npm

> ⚠️ **Not published to npm yet** — this command 404s for now.
>
> ```bash
> dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-token-monitor
> ```

> After installing you must **restart the DSH process once**: the host half is ESM-based and cached, so reloading the plugin will not re-execute it. After that, editing `ui.js` / `config.json` only needs a page refresh.

## Usage

1. A slim tab appears on the right edge showing the balance; hover it to expand the card.
2. The card shows balance / this-conversation tokens / estimated cost, then a grouped breakdown
   (Consumption · Usage · Balance).
3. Drag the tab up or down to move it (remembered as a viewport ratio); click × to collapse, click the tab to reopen.
4. Switch the app language (English / 简体中文) and the widget follows immediately.

> Expansion waits 320 ms of hover, and hovering the × row never expands it, so the close button stays clickable.

## Configuration

`config.json` (next to the plugin, takes effect on page refresh — no restart):

```json
{
  "pollSeconds": 10,
  "balanceSeconds": 60,
  "autoPrices": true,
  "searchPer1000": 5,
  "fetchPer1000": 5,
  "searchBillingFrom": "2026-11-01",
  "prices": {
    "deepseek-flash": {
      "offpeak": { "cacheHit": 0.02, "cacheMiss": 1, "output": 4 },
      "peak":    { "cacheHit": 0.04, "cacheMiss": 2, "output": 8 }
    },
    "deepseek-v4-pro": {
      "offpeak": { "cacheHit": 0.15, "cacheMiss": 4.5, "output": 13.5 },
      "peak":    { "cacheHit": 0.3,  "cacheMiss": 9,   "output": 27 }
    }
  }
}
```

Prices are CNY per million tokens. Peak = Beijing time, weekdays 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00; everything else (weekends included) is half price.

## How the cost is estimated

- The model is read from the session's `requestContext()`, falling back to `deepseek-flash`
- **Each call is priced at the window it happened in**: usage is bucketed into peak / off-peak by event time
- Search / Fetch are billed per request, separately from tokens
- Chinese public holidays are not modelled, so the result is an **estimate**, not an invoice

Prices come from the [official DeepSeek pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/),
scraped monthly into `prices.auto.json` (with `fetchedAt`); a failed scrape keeps the previous values.

## Look and colors

- Tab: brand-blue gradient `#2f7cf6 → #1a5fd0 → #1549a6` with white text; hover adds a white inner ring and a blue glow
- Card: follows the DSH theme tokens (`--dsw-alias-bg-layer-2` / `label-primary` / `label-secondary` / `border-l1`),
  so light and dark switch automatically; built-in light/dark fallbacks are used when tokens are absent
- Status dot: ok = `--dsw-alias-state-success-primary`, pending = `state-warn`, error = `state-error`, idle = `state-idle`
- Numbers are tabular: cost as `≈¥0.42`, tokens as `25.4M tok`

## Permissions & interfaces

It only reads and displays: it never edits sessions, sends messages, or runs Agents. This is the **complete**
list of DSH capabilities it uses.

| Interface (all read-only) | Purpose | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| `ctx.deepseekAccount.getBalance()` | balance + bonus wallet | 60s (`balanceSeconds`) |
| `ctx.sessions.get()` / `list()` | the current session object and live child sessions | 10s |
| `ctx.sessionTitle.get()` | session title (used to follow the active conversation) | 10s |
| `ctx.tokenMeter.measure()` | context usage | 10s |
| `ctx.sessionQuery.traceSession()` | lineage: which child sessions belong to this conversation (reads persisted headers) | 30s / on switch |
| `ctx.sessionQuery.readSession()` | reads a **finished** child session's event log, only to add up tokens | once per child |
| `ctx.agentTeams.tryMembership()` / `listMembers()` | tells teammates apart from ordinary subagents | 10s |
| `ctx.agents.list()` | finds the Agent behind the current session | 10s |

What it registers:

| Registration | Content |
|---|---|
| `webServer.register` | `GET /dsh-token-monitor/state` (balance + usage JSON), `GET /dsh-token-monitor/probe` (diagnostics), `GET /dsh-token-monitor/ui.js` (widget script) |
| `webServer.tapIndex()` (browser mode) / `dsh.client` (desktop) | mounts one same-origin `<script>`; nothing inline |
| Event listeners | `session/event`, `session/disposed`, `subagent/start` — observe only, never intercept or mutate |

Every route passes one auth check first; any one of these admits it: the random token from `token.txt`, a
same-origin / desktop (`dsh-app://app`) Origin, or no Origin at all (local processes, same-origin `fetch`).
Cross-site Origins always get `403` (blocks web pages from reading localhost via CSRF).

**High-risk capabilities it explicitly does NOT use**

- Registers no tools — the model cannot see or call it
- Never writes sessions, mutates events, sends messages, or spawns/interrupts Agents
- Never reads credentials, login tokens, or API keys; does not touch `ctx.credentials` / `ctx.authorization`
- No shell, no subprocesses, no writes outside the package directory
- Never calls `ctx.llm.stream()` — the plugin itself costs nothing

**Can it see my other conversations?** `sessionQuery` spans the whole session corpus, but the plugin only does
two things: `traceSession(currentSession)` to get **its own** subtree, and one log read per **finished** child in
that subtree. It never enumerates the corpus itself, never searches, never reads another conversation's content
(DSH resolves the lineage; the plugin only receives that subtree). Log data is folded into token counters in
memory only — never sent anywhere, never written to disk.

## Privacy

- **Never reads** your login token or API keys
- Balance comes from DSH's own account service (`ctx.deepseekAccount.getBalance()`); the plugin never talks to the platform itself
- **No third-party requests**; the only outbound call is the monthly price-page fetch
- Data lives in process memory plus `localStorage` (tab position only)
- Files written locally: `debug.log` (diagnostics, safe to delete), `token.txt` (page token), `prices.auto.json` (price cache)

## Known limitations

- Counts **one conversation tree only**: the main session plus its subagents and teammates (including their children); other conversations are excluded
- After a subagent or teammate finishes — or after DSH restarts — its spend is back-filled from the on-disk session log; it is lost only if that log is deleted
- Holiday-aware peak detection is not implemented

## Uninstall

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-token-monitor
```

Or: **Settings → Plugins → `dsh-token-monitor` → Uninstall**. Restart DSH once afterwards; the tab disappears.

## Repository layout

```
index.js            host half: balance, usage folding, HTTP routes, price scraping
client.js           client module: mounts ui.js, bridges the app locale
ui.js               the widget itself: plain DOM + Shadow DOM, no build, no deps
cordis.patch.yml    bundle layer: inserts the plugin row
config.json         default configuration
test/smoke.mjs      regression test with a fake ctx (npm test)
test/rollup.mjs     task rollup regression (main session + subagents + teammates)
test/prices.mjs     validates the price parser against the live page
CHANGELOG.md        version history
LICENSE             MIT
```

## Development

```bash
node test/smoke.mjs     # host-half regression with a fake ctx (no DSH needed)
node test/rollup.mjs    # task rollup semantics (main / subagents / teammates)
npm run test:prices     # price parser against the live pricing page
```

Two pitfalls worth knowing:

1. **Inserting a row in a bundle patch requires `insert:`.** `- id: xxx` means "override an existing entry";
   when nothing matches it prints `patch: entry "xxx" not found` and is **silently skipped**.
2. **Route/injection registration must be wrapped in `ctx.effect()`**, otherwise a hot reload leaves the old
   routes registered and the new instance throws `duplicate route`, aborting `apply` halfway.

## Publishing

The repo is pushed through the GitHub REST API (no git needed): `release/<version>/<package>/` becomes one
commit on `main`; older versions stay in `release/<old-version>/` and are not uploaded.

```powershell
# 1) put a GitHub PAT (Contents: Read and write) into .github-token at the repo root
# 2) offline self-check: no network, no token — lists the files and flags runtime artifacts / credentials
$env:GH_DRY = "1"; node tools/push-github.mjs
# 3) real push (commit message defaults to "feat: dsh-token-monitor <version>" from package.json)
node tools/push-github.mjs
```

Remember to set **Topics** (the gear next to About on the repo page):

```
dsh-plugin  dsh  deepseek-harness  deepseek  plugin  token  cost  balance
```

`dsh-plugin` is the primary tag people browse DSH plugins by.
